item.title: How to Stay Safe in Student Accommodation: Essential Tips Every Student Should Know
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Introduction
  2. Always keep your studio safe
  3. Watch Out for Tailgating
  4. Shut Down Windows and Hide Valuables
  5. Use Common Sense When Answering the Door
  6. Take Care of Your Property in Shared Spaces
  7. Report suspicious activity as soon as possible
  8. When necessary, make suggestions for improvements
  9. In conclusion
  10. FAQs

Introduction

Excitement, independence, and a brand-new routine all come with starting uni life. Whether you're relocating to a new city like Preston or living away from home for the first time, student accommodation safety is one of the most important things to understand. While Urban Hub places security at the heart of its operations, every resident plays a role in keeping the community safe.

The good news?

Most safety habits are simple, quick, and become second nature over time. This practical guide explains how to protect your belongings, stay safe, and feel comfortable in your new home.

Always keep your studio safe.

Lock your room, even if you're only stepping away for a minute. It prevents unwanted access and takes only a few seconds. It's fine to keep the door open for friends, but it's not acceptable to leave it open permanently. The entire room comes at risk when a door is propped open.

Watch Out for Tailgating

Tailgating happens when someone enters the building right behind you without using their own key or fob.

If you feel comfortable, politely ask, “Who are you visiting?”
If anything feels suspicious, notify the on-site team immediately. Urban Hub’s staff are trained to check and act promptly as part of our accommodation safety procedures.

Close Windows and Keep Valuables Out of Sight

Before leaving your room, ensure your windows are closed. Opportunistic theft can occur even on upper floors if a window is left open.

Keep valuables such as laptops, wallets, and phones away from windowsills or shelves visible from outside.

Be Cautious When Answering the Door

If someone knocks unexpectedly, always ask who it is before opening.
If you’re unsure or feel uncomfortable:

• Keep the door closed
• Ask them to return later
• Contact the Urban Hub team for help

Your safety comes first; trust your instincts.

Take Care of Your Property in Shared Spaces

Shared areas such as lounges, study rooms, and communal kitchens are convenient but require awareness. Always keep personal items close and never leave valuables unattended.

Avoid placing keys near the entrance of your studio, as they are the easiest items for intruders to pick up quickly.

Report suspicious activity immediately

If something doesn’t feel right, rely on your intuition. Report unusual behaviour or unknown individuals to security staff or reception.

Urban Hub’s team handles these matters discreetly and efficiently. Early reporting helps prevent bigger issues and keeps the community safer

Suggest Improvements When Needed

If you notice an area that could benefit from extra lighting, improved locks, or clearer signage, speak up. Resident feedback is essential for maintaining a safe environment. Urban Hub listens to all safety-related suggestions as part of its continuous improvement approach.

In conclusion,

How to stay safe in student accommodation?

Living at Urban Hub is designed to be safe, comfortable, and worry-free. With secure access, CCTV, on-site assistance, and a friendly community, you’re already starting from a strong foundation.

But small daily habits, locking doors, staying alert, and safeguarding valuables, complete the safety circle.

With the right awareness and responsibility, your stay at Urban Hub becomes not only comfortable but confidently secure, giving you peace of mind throughout your university experience.

FAQs

1. How safe is student accommodation, and what security features should I look for?

In general, student housing is highly safe, and Urban Hub is no different. To ensure the safety of its residents, Urban Hub provides secure entry, CCTV, on-site staff, and adequate lighting throughout the building.

2. Do student accommodations have CCTV, key-card access, or on-site security staff?

Sure. Urban Hub provides round-the-clock safety and assistance featuring CCTV in strategic locations, secure key-card entry, and a dedicated on-site staff.

3. Is it safe to live alone in a studio as a student?

Urban Hub's studios are ideal for students who prefer independent living, as they are built with safety and privacy in mind. We provide monitored facilities, secure entry, and on-site support.

4. What are the primary security tips for university accommodation?

Use the 24-hour emergency hotline provided at check-in, or contact the on-site team right away if you feel that something is not right. Your alertness in situations is the most valuable input you can provide!

5. How can I keep my belongings, including laptops and valuables?

Avoid leaving anything unattended in public areas, keep your door closed, and conceal valuables. Urban Hub's CCTV monitoring also provides an additional layer of security, ensuring every place is under surveillance.

item.title: Best Healthcare Apps for Students: Top Recommendations and Why You Need Them
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Introduction
  2. Why Are Healthcare Apps Important for Students?
  3. Healthcare Apps' Advantages for Urban Hub Students
  4. Conclusion
  5. FAQs

Introduction

It's not always simple to manage your health while you're a student. Tight deadlines, late-night revision sessions, and a new way of living away from home can all cause your well-being to fall off the list of priorities. At Urban Hub, we recognise that independent life comes with new obligations and maintaining one's health ought to be among the easiest. The way young people monitor their health, seek expert advice, and create balanced lifestyles has been revolutionised by healthcare apps. These student wellness apps can be helpful when you're studying, whether it's for scheduling virtual GP appointments or keeping an eye on your sleep patterns. The top healthcare apps that students should think about are discussed below, along with the reasons why they are so helpful, particularly if you live in a welcoming, student-focused community like Urban Hub in Preston.

Why Are Healthcare Apps Important for Students?

Avoiding disease is only one aspect of staying healthy; another is preserving the vitality, concentration, and stability required to succeed in academic and social situations. Students benefit from healthcare apps in several important ways:
  • Convenience: Get expert assistance anytime, anywhere.
  • Prevention: Use monitoring tools to stay ahead of possible health problems.
  • Mental well-being: During crucial academic times, receive guided care and support.
  • Be prepared for emergencies: by keeping vital medical information close at hand.
  • Routine Building: Use trackers and reminders to create healthy behaviours.

1. NHS- National Health Service

  • It is the publicly funded healthcare system in the UK that provides basic medical services at minimal or no cost.
  • It makes well-being easier and more affordable for university students by offering free GP consultations, emergency care, mental health assistance, medicines at standard rates, and convenient access to healthcare through the NHS App.

2. Patient Access

Patient Access is a widely used UK healthcare app that allows students to stay connected with their GP practice anytime.
  • The app makes it easy to book GP appointments, helping you avoid lengthy wait times or phone queues, particularly on busy university days.
  • If you rely on regular medication and don’t want to miss a dose during a check-up, the app can help you get repeat prescriptions and track your prescriptions.
  • Additionally, you may examine your medical information, such as test results and immunisation records, which makes it simpler to maintain structured health records when living away from home.
  • Patient Access frequently offers extra features that enhance your convenience and flexibility, even if your GP surgery is not fully integrated with the NHS App.

3. The Medical & Mental Health Apps like- Unmind and NowPatient

  • With a classic benefit of upfront pricing, they are the top mental health apps for students on a tight budget because there are no unexpected costs.
  • For mental health or stress management, these apps connect you with accredited therapists who, in turn, offer some of the best stress care available in the UK.
  • They are an excellent option for non-emergency conditions such as infections, allergies, and flu.

4. Your Fitness Partner: Anytime Fitness

  • This app connects you with the nearest Anytime Fitness facilities, so you don’t have to compromise your gym routine.
  • Through the app, you can get exercise, nutrition, and mindfulness advice.
  • Students love it because it is an easy way to maintain an active lifestyle without being limited by time or location.

5. Emergency Health Information, or Medical ID

  • Lock-screen Profiles: It is one of the best healthcare apps for university students, which lets first responders view your critical medical information.
  • In an emergency, it automatically notifies a few of your chosen contacts about your location.
  • Particularly helpful for students living away from home for the first time, it is one of the most essential apps you will ever need on your mobile phone.

6. Flo: Period & Health Tracker for Women

  • Flo uses artificial intelligence to accurately predict PMS, ovulation, and menstrual cycles for women.
  • It also helps you understand how your cycle is affected by stress, sleep, and lifestyle choices.
  • It is one of the most beneficial apps for female students or women during busy academic times when cycles could change.

7. NHS Prescriptions: Pharmacy2U

  • The largest NHS-approved prescription delivery business in the UK, Pharmacy2U, is well-liked among university students who want easy access to medicine.
  • During hectic university weeks or bad weather, the app makes it possible for you to obtain your NHS prescriptions online and have them delivered straight to your home.
  • When visiting a physical pharmacy is inconvenient, it saves students time and money by providing free delivery for NHS prescriptions.
  • To ensure you never run out during exams, deadlines, or when you're ill, the app reminds you when it's time to reorder your prescription.
  • Students can feel secure knowing that their medications are handled properly and safely because they are fully NHS-approved.

8. Sleepio

Sleepio is a science-based digital sleep software that helps enhance overall sleep health through cognitive behavioural techniques. Why is it beneficial to students:
  • It offers structured guidance to help establish better routines and re-establish late-night sleep cycles.
  • It enhances mood, energy, and sleep quality, all of which help improve academic focus.
  • Most students can use it for free thanks to partnerships with the NHS and many universities.

Healthcare Apps' Advantages for Urban Hub Students

  • Students can use apps to track their progress, monitor symptoms, and gain a deeper understanding of their bodies.
  • Concentration naturally improves with better sleep, less stress, and a healthy diet.
  • Support is always available, whether you're struggling with anxiety, burnout, or a cold.
  • Many apps are inexpensive or free, making them ideal for students on a tight budget.
  • Apps encourage students to eat healthier, stay active, drink plenty of fluids, and, most importantly, get enough sleep.

Conclusion:

Health and wellness apps for college students 2025: One Easy Step Can Start Your Well-Being Living at Urban Hub entails living in a welcoming setting that puts your comfort and way of life first. When you combine that with the right healthcare apps, you have everything you need to maintain your well-being throughout your academic journey. These apps surely help make student life easier, safer, and more balanced, whether you're managing stress, improving sleep, or simply keeping an eye on your health. Discover these apps, stay informed and take charge of your health today to make your time as a student at Urban Hub healthier than ever.

FAQs

1. Which healthcare apps are most recommended for UK university students?

Popular apps among UK students include NHS App, Headspace, Student Health App, Calm, and MyFitnessPal. These apps support everything from mental well-being to symptom checking and daily health tracking, making them ideal for student life.

2. Are AI-powered healthcare apps reliable for checking symptoms or getting medical guidance?

AI health apps can be reliable for early guidance, symptom checking, and lifestyle advice. However, they do not replace a GP or NHS healthcare professional. They are best used as supportive tools to help students make informed decisions more quickly.

3. What free mental-health and well-being apps do UK students use the most?

UK students frequently use NHS Every Mind Matters, Headspace (student version), Calm, MindShift, and Happify. These apps offer breathing exercises, guided meditation, stress support, mood tracking, and AI-powered well-being suggestions.

4. Can AI health apps replace visits to the GP or NHS Walk-In Centres for students?

No—AI apps cannot replace a GP or NHS clinical visit. They can, however, analyse symptoms, provide preliminary advice, and help students understand whether they need urgent care. They work best as a first step, rather than a comprehensive medical diagnosis.

5. How do AI health-tracking apps help students manage stress, sleep, and daily routines?

AI tools monitor patterns in sleep, stress, hydration, heart rate, and activity levels. They use this data to offer personalised recommendations, helping students maintain better routines, reduce burnout, and stay healthy during busy academic periods.

item.title: Do International Students Need Health Insurance? Top 10 Benefits Explained
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Why international students need health insurance in the UK
  2. The Top 10 benefits of medical insurance for overseas students
  3. In conclusion
  4. FAQs

It's normal for health insurance to fall to the bottom of your to-do list when you're juggling courses, exploring the city, and getting used to campus life.

Why international students need health insurance in the UK

It's normal for health insurance to fall to the bottom of your to-do list when you're juggling courses, exploring the city, and getting used to campus life. The reality is that health insurance is a vital protection rather than just a formality, especially when you’re in a completely new place. Living abroad isn't always just a rosy picture. Settling into a new country involves many practical considerations, from accommodation and food shopping to travel and daily expenses. Amidst all the planned things, there are still many beyond your control. It may include unforeseen expenses, medical emergencies and sometimes uncontrollable situations. Health insurance guarantees that you obtain prompt medical attention without worrying about money, regardless of the severity of the illness, from a minor viral infection to a serious sports injury. Here are the top 10 advantages, presented in an easy-to-understand manner, to assist you in understanding why international students should think about trustworthy health insurance.

The Top 10 Benefits of Medical Insurance for overseas students

1. Quicker Treatment Access

  • Private health insurance often enables faster access to medical care.
  • If you choose health insurance, you benefit from faster diagnosis and better recovery outcomes, thanks to shorter waiting times.
  • It is beneficial when you can't afford lengthy delays, such as during emergencies or exam season.

2. Quick Diagnostics & Specialist Appointments

  • You can get tests, scans, and specialists more quickly if you have insurance.
  • Early diagnosis helps prevent conditions from worsening.
  • Quick diagnostics and early treatment keep you healthy so you can enjoy life at Urban Hub and concentrate on your university studies and work.

3. Complete Protection Against Serious Illnesses

  • Numerous plans offer comprehensive coverage for critical illnesses and conditions, including cancer, with advanced therapies, chemotherapy, and surgery.
  • Opting for health insurance helps lessen your financial burden and provides you with access to the best medical care when it counts most.

4. Availability of Private Hospital Rooms

  • During treatment, benefit from a quieter setting, comfort, and privacy.
  • Improved rest and reduced infection risk help accelerate healing.
  • An enormous benefit if you need a quiet place and are far from home.

5. Online Doctor's Appointments

  • Many UK insurance providers offer video consultations with licensed General Practitioners (GPs).
  • These online consultations are perfect for brief check-ups, mild illnesses, and prescription renewals.
  • It saves students time and prevents unnecessary travel, which is especially helpful on hectic university days.
  • You must have some widely used health apps on your mobile in the UK as of 2025 for an enhanced consultation experience, such as the NHS app, Patient Access, NowPatient, and more.

6. Assistance with Mental Health

  • Mental health services such as patient counselling and therapy are often included.
  • The coverage for mental health balance helps manage academic pressure, homesickness, culture shock, and stress.
  • It is vital for preserving emotional health when living away from home.
  • Assistance for mental health concerns can also be accessed through online applications such as Wysa, Headspace, Unmind, and others.

7. Best health insurance options for international students

  • When you have health insurance, you can select the hospitals, clinics, and specialists you prefer, without worrying about the finances.
  • You can look for a doctor's appointment around your university, part-time employment, or gym sessions when you have flexibility.
  • This gives you greater control over how you receive medical care.

8. Preventive Medical Examinations

  • Many health insurance plans cover annual screenings and regular check-ups.
  • Complications can be avoided by identifying problems early through these medical examinations, such as diabetes or hypertension.
  • It encourages students to keep up long-term healthy routines.

9. Advantages of Wellness

  • Specific insurance policies offer discounts on fitness apps, wellness programmes, and gym memberships.
  • It promotes an active lifestyle, which is ideal for students attempting to manage their well-being, social lives, and academic commitments.
  • An excellent addition to Urban Hub's community-driven atmosphere.

10. Emergency Medical Cover

  • One must acknowledge that sudden illnesses and accidents can occur at any time with anyone. Without insurance, emergency care is frequently costly. In such situations, health insurance shields you from overwhelming medical costs, so you can focus on recovering rather than worrying about the cost.

In conclusion

Having health insurance guarantees that you are safe, supported, and free to concentrate on making the most of your time as a student in Preston. Student insurance must not be considered an expense; instead, it is one of the best investments you can make for your safety and peace of mind. So, make it a priority whether you're moving into your new studio or getting ready for your first day of university. Start your journey with confidence!

FAQs

1. Do international students in the UK need private health insurance if they already pay the NHS Health Surcharge

Not always. Although the NHS surcharge provides full access to NHS services, some students opt for private insurance to obtain additional coverage or expedited appointments.

2. What is the difference between NHS access and private health insurance for international students in the UK

While private insurance provides faster access to specialists, private hospitals, dental coverage, and additional wellness perks, the NHS covers basic healthcare.

3. How can AI-powered health apps help international students track symptoms, appointments, and insurance claims

AI health apps can help you manage private insurance claims, monitor symptoms, schedule visits, and provide basic medical advice all in one location.

4. Is travel insurance enough for international students studying in the UK long-term

No, travel insurance is meant for brief excursions. Long-term students should expect access to the NHS and, if necessary, additional private health insurance.

5. What medical expenses are not covered by the NHS that international students should know about before arriving in the UK

The majority of dental treatment, eye examinations, glasses, private consultations, and certain immunisations are not covered by the NHS. These usually have to be paid for separately by students.

item.title: Christmas in Preston: Spending Christmas in Student Accommodation
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Introduction
  2. Make Your Space a Winter Wonderland
  3. What Students Do in Preston at Christmas
  4. Create Your Own Christmas Traditions
  5. Movies for Christmas, but Make It a Marathon
  6. Feel Connected and Give Back
  7. A Special Christmas Despite Being Different

Introduction

As the first semester wraps up and festive playlists start playing everywhere, it can only mean one thing: Christmas in Preston has arrived!

While many students head home for the holidays, you might be one of those who plan to stay put in your student accommodation in Preston this winter. It can be a bittersweet experience to spend Christmas away from home; exciting, yet a little strange. Preston has everything you need to make your holiday season memorable, unique, comfortable, and unexpectedly unforgettable.

Make Your Space a Winter Wonderland

Christmas begins with atmosphere, and your studio is the ideal place to create it. It's your time to add a festive yet personal touch to your space. The atmosphere can be instantly lifted with a small Christmas tree, sparkling fairy lights, or even a few festive cushions.

There are several reasonably priced stores in Preston's city centre, such as B&M and Home Bargains, so you don't have to go over budget. If you enjoy getting crafty, you can also make your own decorations.

What Students Do in Preston at Christmas

Even if Preston is comparatively quieter during the holiday period, the city's charm is undeniable during Christmas. On chilly winter evenings, the city's Christmas markets and seasonal activities offer a perfect mix of warmth and festive excitement. A simple way to experience the Christmas mood is to take a stroll around the Flag Market, which has food stalls, hot drinks, and seasonal music.

Enjoy the simple pleasure of strolling down the street with a hot chocolate in hand, meeting new people, making friends, and staying warm. The little things often give the season its magic and make it feel truly comforting.

Create Your Own Christmas Traditions

Being able to create your own customs is one of the best aspects of staying in student housing during Christmas holidays. You can organise a communal Christmas dinner with your flatmates; it doesn't necessarily need to be elaborate to be festive, whether it's a simple shared meal at your place or sitting down together for some fun activities.

Student kitchens are ideal for vegetarian nut roasts, pasta bakes, and turkey sandwiches. Making a gingerbread house or a batch of festive brownies may also turn into an evening full of music, laughter, and friendly rivalry if baking is more your style.

Movies for Christmas, but Make It a Marathon

Spending Christmas in student accommodation in Preston definitely calls for a film night, as it is one of the best ways to feel cosy, just like when you're home!

Get some popcorn, pull out the blankets, and settle in for a marathon of Christmas films. There is something for everyone, from Home Alone and Elf to Love Actually (or even Die Hard, if you're daring). Watching alongside your flatmates and friends makes the occasion cosier and reminds us that Christmas is about more than just where you spend it.

Feel Connected and Give Back

Volunteering is another fantastic way to spend your holiday doing something worthwhile during student holidays UK. Over Christmas, Preston's local charities frequently require extra help, and volunteering your time can be immensely rewarding.

Giving back to others can shift your perspective and make the season feel more fulfilling, richer, and more connected, without making you feel sad about not being home.

A Special Christmas Despite Being Different

Student accommodation Christmas celebrations don't have to be depressing or lonely for students who can't make it home during this holiday season. You can make it an unforgettable Christmas with a bit of ingenuity, fantastic company, and the allure of Preston surrounding you.

At UrbanHub, your accommodation should feel like home year-round, not just during the academic year. We hope this Christmas, wherever you are, is full of love, joy, and treasured memories.

item.title: Do Students Pay Council Tax in the UK? All You Need to Know
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Council Tax: What Is It?
  2. Student council tax? Do you need to pay?
  3. What Happens If You Live in a UK Student Housing?
  4. Students Living with Family or After Graduation
  5. What About Students Who Attend Classes Part-Time?
  6. How to Get a Council Tax Exemption
  7. Essential Things to Keep in Mind
  8. To sum up!
  9. FAQs

Same budget, but new expenses; it's very common!

It may be challenging to manage finances as a student in the UK, particularly when new bills start coming in. Do students pay council tax in the UK? - one of the most frequently asked questions. Although council tax is typically a family expense, students are covered by different, and often more favourable, rules. You can avoid stress and unexpected expenses by knowing when you are exempt from the bills, when you might have to pay, and how to ask for discounts. So, without further ado, let's break it all down!

Council Tax: What Is It?

In England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland, councils are responsible for collecting a local tax known as council tax. It contributes towards funding vital community services in the UK, including social services, libraries, fire and police services, street lighting, and waste collection. The local council's rates and the property's valuation band determine the amount to be charged. Unless they are eligible for an exemption or discount, every household is responsible for paying their council tax.

Student council tax? Do you need to pay?

Depending on your course status and who you live with, full-time students typically do not have to pay council tax. The student accommodation you have opted for is entirely exempt from council tax if every resident in the accommodation is a full-time student. This holds for many university residence halls, shared accommodation, and purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA). But things are different if you live with people who aren't students. Non-student residents are usually responsible for the cost, and the household will not be eligible for a full exemption. If they are the only liable adult, they qualify for a 25% single-person discount.

What Happens If You Live in a UK Student Housing?

The majority of university residence halls and purpose-built student housing (PBSA) are automatically exempt from council tax. The landlord or accommodation provider, not the students, has responsibility in these situations. This is one of the reasons why the council tax exemption for international students is simpler, more reliable, and cost-effective if you have opted for student accommodation in the UK. Council tax is usually not a concern at Urban Hub, as student life is designed to be as hassle-free as possible. There are no hidden charges with us!

Students Living with Family or After Graduation

You are not directly responsible for council tax if you live with your family, and you are not counted as a liable adult since you are a student. The bill is still your parents' or guardians' responsibility. Your student exemption expires on the official course end date if you graduate or drop out of your course. Unless there is another exemption, you may be subject to paying council tax. It's essential to inform the council if you continue living in student housing after graduation to avoid backdated penalties.

What About Students Who Attend Classes Part-Time?

Council tax is not waived for part-time students. Council tax is usually charged in full, subject to any other applicable discounts, if all members of the family work part-time or are not students.

How to Get a Council Tax Exemption

It's essential to apply as soon as you move in or begin your course because council tax exemptions are not granted automatically. There is a process, and it can take some time to be approved. You can apply online for the majority of councils. To apply, you'll need:
  • A certificate of enrolment or student status from your university
  • Your proof of address or tenancy agreement
  • Proof of identity, if required

Once you enrol, universities send council tax exemption letters that you can give straight to the council.

Essential Things to Keep in Mind

  • Students who live with other students full-time are typically exempt.
  • Council tax may be due if you live with non-students.
  • Generally, student housing and residence halls are exempt.
  • Always let the council know if your situation changes.

To sum up!

So, in the UK, do students pay council tax? The answer is no for the majority of full-time students, but only if the appropriate exemptions are in place. Your money can be saved and unnecessary costs avoided if your accommodation provider follows all council tax rules for student accommodation UK. You can also avoid extra charges by staying alert and informed about the regulations and applying as soon as possible. Financial management can be much simplified by selecting the ideal student housing. We're pleased to share that Urban Hub is one of the student housing destinations where additional charges are never applied. With our backing, you can focus on your academics and enjoy student life with peace of mind. For more information, get in touch with us!

FAQs

1. Do full-time students need to pay council tax in the UK?

In most cases, no. Full-time students are usually exempt from paying council tax, especially when living in student accommodation, halls of residence, or purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA). At Urban Hub, council tax is one less thing you need to worry about.

2. What if I live with non-students?

If you share a home with non-students, the household may not qualify for a full council tax exemption. In such cases, the non-student residents are typically responsible for the bill and may be eligible for a single-person discount. Choosing dedicated student accommodation like Urban Hub helps avoid these complications.

3. Are international students exempt from council tax?

Yes, international students studying full-time in the UK are entitled to the same council tax exemptions as UK students. When you stay in recognised student accommodation, such as Urban Hub, the process is straightforward and stress-free.

4. Do part-time students have to pay council tax?

Part-time students are generally required to pay council tax, although some discounts may apply depending on individual circumstances. If you are unsure, it’s always best to check with your local council or accommodation provider.

5. How does Urban Hub make council tax simple for students?

At Urban Hub, council tax is already taken care of for eligible students. There are no hidden charges or unexpected bills, allowing you to focus on your studies and enjoy university life with complete peace of mind.

item.title: How International Students Can Secure Accommodation Before Arriving in the UK
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Introduction
  2. Book student accommodation before arriving in UK
  3. Understand the Different Kinds of Student Housing
  4. Select the Appropriate Type of Room
  5. Establish a Reasonable Budget
  6. Pay Close Attention to the Location of UK student housing
  7. Use social media for any additional information
  8. Recognise the Support System and Contract
  9. UK student housing for international students - In Conclusion
  10. FAQs

Introduction

The idea of relocating to the UK for your studies sounds fantastic. Still, finding suitable accommodation before you get there may be difficult, particularly if you're travelling to a new country. This situation calls for some research on the student’s part!

Early planning is essential for a student, right from reviewing contracts to budgeting wisely and understanding different types of accommodation. Finding the ideal place to live is necessary for international students, as it affects their entire academic journey and goes beyond simple convenience.

To give you peace of mind from the moment you arrive, we at Urban Hub outline, through this blog guide, the practical steps to help you understand how international students secure accommodation in Preston, UK.

Book student accommodation before arriving in UK

Booking early is always advantageous for international students. As accommodation providers, we advise students to start exploring options as soon as they receive their university offer. By doing so, you can get:

  • More options, better locations, and often better prices are available with early reservations.
  • Delaying your search may limit availability, as popular student cities often see high demand.
  • If you don't apply for university housing, universities typically presume you’ll find private accommodation.
  • You may examine choices calmly and avoid last-minute stress by starting early.

Understand the Different Kinds of Student Housing

While you begin your search, make sure you try to understand the primary international student accommodation options in the UK before making a choice:

On-campus housing:

  • Located on or near the university campus
  • Perfect for first-year students
  • Usually reserved for the entire academic year or has shorter tenancy periods.

Private accommodation:

  • Offers more flexibility in terms of stay, contract duration and location.
  • May accommodate both working professionals and students, or may be specifically for students?

PBSA, or purpose-built student housing:

  • Specifically created for students
  • Includes community areas, study spaces, gyms, and on-site support.
  • Adaptable rental durations and room types

Because of their ease, security, and student-focused amenities, PBSAs are especially popular among international students.

Select the Appropriate Type of Room

Your budget, lifestyle, and privacy preferences should all be considered when selecting a UK student housing and must include factors like:

Shared Rooms:

  • More social and reasonably priced
  • In the UK, offer less privacy but a more social ambience

Private rooms:

  • Your own bedroom, occasionally with an en-suite bathroom
  • Common areas and a shared kitchen
  • The most popular option among students in the UK

Studio apartments:

  • Fully self-contained living space
  • Higher price, making them perfect for people who value independence

Establish a Reasonable Budget

  • Understand how your university life will be, and how much you can afford to spend each month before committing to any accommodation.
  • Take into account living expenses, such as food and transport, in addition to rent.
  • To prevent unforeseen costs, look for all-inclusive bills.
  • Keep in mind that many accommodation providers require a deposit, often equal to one month's rent, so be prepared to provide it.
  • Clarity on the budget will also help narrow down options beyond your expense list and avoid future financial hardship.

Pay Close Attention to the Location of UK student housing

Your location greatly influences your student experience. Consider the following aspects when you check the location of your housing, as it will help you understand the practicality of your accommodation from any other everyday needs:

  • How far is your campus from your place of residence?
  • Is it simple to use public transport?
  • Are you able to ride a bike or walk to university?
  • How simple is it to get to the town centre, shops, and public areas?

Particularly during busy academic weeks, a well-located home saves time, money, and energy.

Use social media for any additional information

Use the following digital resources if you are unable to visit in person:

  • Examine images and videos closely.
  • Utilise the virtual tours that many accommodation providers offer.
  • Check for the common areas, storage space, and room layouts of your accommodation for better clarity.

By doing this, you can ensure the property meets your expectations before you get there.

Recognise the Support System and Contract

Read the contract carefully before signing it:

  • Verify the payment terms and the required deposit.
  • Understand the cancellation policies, particularly when a visa is delayed.
  • Check who to contact in case of emergency or maintenance issues.

UK student housing for international students - In Conclusion

It doesn't have to be challenging to find a place to live before travelling to the UK. International students can also choose an accommodation that supports both academic performance and personal comfort with confidence if they do all their research in advance, stick to a clear budget, and contact accommodation providers for all the details.

Student housing at Urban Hub is designed to be easy, safe, and encouraging, so you can focus on settling into life in the UK and making the most of your time at university. We understand the concerns students may have, and we are located precisely where students need us. We ensure that your stay with us is no less than you have imagined and what we have promised.

We hope this guide has cleared the clouds and provided you with insights on securing a good deal on accommodation. For any further updates, you can write to our team, and we shall get back to you!

FAQs

1. When should foreign students make hotel reservations in the UK?

In order to obtain better locations, rates, and availability, international students should begin looking for housing as soon as they receive their university offer.

2. What kinds of housing options are there for students in the UK?

There are three options available to students: private living, on-campus housing, and purpose-built student housing (PBSA), each of which offers varying degrees of comfort, support, and flexibility.

3. What kind of room is ideal for students from other countries?

The most common option is a private room since it provides privacy while maintaining access to communal spaces. Students who want complete independence can benefit from studios.

4. What should students budget for when it comes to housing?

To prevent unforeseen costs, students should budget for food, transport, deposits, and make sure bills are covered in addition to rent.

5. Why is location crucial when selecting housing for students in the UK?

Time is saved, travel expenses are decreased, and student life is made more convenient by a well-located property near university, public transportation, and local attractions.

item.title: How Can International Students Get a UK Driving Licence? Step-by-Step Guide
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Introduction
  2. Fundamental Qualifications for an International student driving
  3. Students with a valid home country licence in the UK
  4. How to Apply for a Provisional Driving Licence in the UK?
  5. UK driving licence process for foreign students
  6. Preparing for the Practical Test
  7. After Passing Your Test
  8. In conclusion
  9. FAQs

Introduction

As an international student, relocating to the UK can lead to new experiences, friendships, and independence. Even though public transport in the UK is reliable and well-connected, many students eventually want something more flexible—especially for weekend trips, late study sessions, part-time jobs, or simply exploring nearby cities. Having a car gives you a whole new level of independence.

Being based in the heart of Preston makes it even easier for international students living at Urban Hub to travel comfortably. However, you must learn how to obtain a UK driving licence before you get behind the wheel. When broken down, the process is far easier than you might imagine, even though it may initially look complicated.

This student guide will take you through every step of the process, including eligibility, paperwork, tests, and key regulations, so that you can drive legally and with confidence.

Fundamental Qualifications for an International Student Driving in the UK

Before applying, confirm that you fulfil the necessary legal requirements:

Eligibility Requirements include:

  • To apply for a provisional driving licence, you have to be at least 17 years old.
  • You must be normally resident in the UK for at least 185 days in any 12 months.
  • From twenty metres away, you should be able to read a number plate.

Driving Requirements under the Law of the UK include:

  • A current UK driving licence, either full or provisional.
  • Insurance for the car you drive.
  • A vehicle that has valid road tax and a current MOT, if necessary.
  • It needs to be registered in the United Kingdom.

Students with a valid home country licence in the UK

As of 2025, the UK has a few designated nations. You can drive in the UK for a whole year if you have a licence from any of these DVLA-approved countries:

  • Australia
  • Canada
  • New Zealand
  • Japan
  • Singapore
  • South Korea
  • South Africa
  • Switzerland
  • Hong Kong
  • And some others (e.g., Gibraltar, Jersey, Guernsey, Isle of Man)

After a year, you must either apply for a UK driving licence or, if your country is eligible, swap your current one.

Students in EEA vs. Non-EEA

  • Holders of EEA Licences: There is no need for a new exam; your licence is still valid.
  • Non-EEA Students: After obtaining a BRP and proof of address, international students can apply right away.

How to Apply for a Provisional Driving Licence in the UK?

It’s easy to apply for a provisional licence online. Here’s what you need to do next.

  • Go to the official GOV.UK website and complete the application.
  • Make the £34 online payment.
  • Make sure you are of legal age.

You must make a note of the following documents:

  • A valid passport is proof of identity.
  • Address history in the UK
  • Evidence of residency (if requested)
  • Passport-style photo, if necessary

Upon completing the application process, your provisional licence will be posted to you. Throughout your university life, you must always have it with you.

UK driving licence process for foreign students

For international students, there are two tests: the Theory Test and the Practical Test. Clearing both tests is necessary to obtain a full UK licence.

A. Theory Test

The following make up the theory test:

  • Multiple-choice questions about the Highway Code
  • Hazard perception test using video clips

To be ready for this examination, you need to learn:

  • The Highway Code
  • Recognise traffic signs
  • Driving: essential skills
  • Eyesight rules: must read a number plate at 20 metres

To appear in this examination, you need to:

  • Book online at GOV.UK.
  • £23 is the test fee.

This confirms your booking for the test day. You must take your provisional licence with you to the test centre.

B. Practical Driving Test

Once you pass the theory test, you move ahead to the practical test. This test requires your knowledge of:

  • Vehicle safety questions (“Show me, tell me”)
  • General driving skills
  • Manoeuvres
  • Independent driving section

The test formalities include:

  • £62 for a weekday test
  • Additional cost for weekend/evening slots

Vehicle Requirements

The vehicle you use for your daily commute must also comply with UK law. The car must:

  • Display L-plates on the car
  • Be insured for learner drivers.
  • It should be compliant with the existing road requirements.

Preparing for the Practical Test

Can international students drive in the UK? If you would like to prepare for the practical test, you can go about it in the following two ways-

A Driving Instructor

  • He must be DVSA-approved
  • He must be able to deliver professional guidance.
  • He must have access to dual-control vehicles.

A Family Member or Friend

The supervising driver must:

  • Be 21 or older
  • Hold a full UK/EEA licence for at least 3 years.
  • Be qualified to drive the same type of vehicle.

After Passing Your Test

If you clear both the tests, congratulations!

After you pass the examinations, you will be issued a full UK driving licence valid for 10 years. You can update your insurance coverage after the licence is issued. Also, if you want other drivers to be aware of your recent qualification, you can display your P-plates on the vehicle.

In conclusion,

As an Urban Hub resident, you already live in a cohesive, student-focused community. In addition to that, you will be even more prepared to enjoy life in Preston once you have your licence. If you are new to the UK and want to know how to apply for a UK driving licence as an international student, get your provisional licence as of now, schedule your study and driving lessons, appear for the examination and get ready to experience true independence on the road!

FAQs

1. Can international students apply for a UK driving licence while on a student visa?

Indeed. If an international student meets the residency requirements and has a valid biometric residence permit (BRP), they can apply for a provisional driving licence in the UK.

2. What documents do international students need to get a UK provisional driving licence?

Your BRP, passport, proof of address, and, if you have one, your National Insurance number are usually required. The DVLA accepts online applications.

3. How long can international students drive on their foreign licence in the UK before switching to a UK licence?

The majority of international students can use their foreign licence for up to 12 months after arrival. They then need to apply for a licence in the UK.

4. How can international students pass the UK theory test quickly? Are there recommended apps or tools?

Frequent use of DVSA-approved apps is very beneficial. For rapid review, many students use Theory Test Pro, Driving Test Success, or the official DVSA Theory Test Kit.

5. What is the full step-by-step process for international students to convert their foreign driving licence to a UK licence?

Applying for a provisional licence, passing the theory test, taking driving lessons and completing the practical test are all requirements. Your UK driving licence is issued by the DVLA once you pass the test.

item.title: Networking Tips for Students: 11 Proven Ways to Build Connections and Boost Your Career
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Introduction
  2. But, is it really worth it?
  3. How can students improve their networking skills?
  4. FAQs

Introduction

Today, it takes more than just technical proficiency and grades to secure your ideal career. Who you know can frequently be just as essential as what you know in a competitive job market. Networking helps students and young graduates gain access to jobs, industry insights, internships, mentorships, and, in some cases, visa-sponsored positions.

But, is it really worth it?

Developing solid professional relationships early on can give your career a significant advantage, whether you've recently moved into a student accommodation like Urban Hub or are adjusting to life as a student in the UK. Below are 11 practical and proven networking strategies to help university students build a strong professional circle. So, without further ado, let's break it down!

1. Establish Early Connections: Networking tips

  • Don't put things off until you need them. Long before job applications start, building professional connections early is one of the most valuable steps you can take for your future.
  • Participate in campus mixers, join societies, talk to classmates, and have casual conversations with peers.
  • As for your place of residence, the common spaces at Urban Hub inevitably foster discussions that may serve as the cornerstone of your future professional network.

2. Before you approach someone, do some research.

  • Examine their latest projects, published work, and LinkedIn profile.
  • Make thoughtful enquiries about the people you look up to. This makes you stand out and demonstrates sincere interest.
  • Make the conversation personal. Talking about your accomplishments enhances conversations and gives you an edge over others.

3. Put Relationship Building First

  • Building relationships rather than gathering contacts is the essence of true networking.
  • Provide support, seize opportunities, or share valuable resources.
  • Appreciate your network of peers. Many students at Urban Hub come from diverse backgrounds; your flatmate today can be your business partner tomorrow.

4. Honour Every Relationship

  • Don't base your decisions on titles and designations. You never know who might outshine others in the future.
  • Make meaningful queries and express gratitude for everyone's experiences.
  • When you make someone feel important, people are more inclined to assist you in your journey.

5. Maintain an Open Mind, as it is always good for career networking

  • Go beyond your area of expertise and expand your horizons. Unexpected paths often lead to some of the best chances you'll ever get in life.
  • Adopt a multidisciplinary approach. Today's industries combine expertise from other fields, such as business and psychology, technology and design, and more.
  • Diversify your networks to get diverse opportunities.

6. Establish an Online Identity

  • Make good use of LinkedIn.
  • Observe leaders in the sector.
  • Interact with posts
  • Talk about your personal observations.
  • Use X (formerly Twitter).
  • Share your remarks on threads.
  • Participate in academic or business communities.
  • Take part in alumni and student organisations.

All these tips for growing your career network as a student will keep you visible in the public eye and allow you to interact with like-minded people.

7. Go to Webinars and Events

  • The best places to network are career fairs, industry panels, guest lectures, and social gatherings.
  • To get noticed during Q&A sessions, be attentive and ask meaningful questions.
  • Meet alumni and businesspeople by attending speed-networking events hosted by your university.
  • To establish a long-lasting relationship, follow up with your connections later.

8. Set Up Informational Conversations

  • Speak with experts you respect. You can gain clarity on roles and sectors through a brief virtual or in-person conversation.
  • Use these meet-ups to understand corporate culture. This is very useful before submitting applications.
  • A successful informational interview may also result in future recommendations or mentorship offers.

9. Have Sincere Discussions

  • Avoid pre-planned small conversations.
  • Talk about your passions, objectives, and driving forces.
  • Engage in active listening; genuine, captivating discussions are much more memorable than practised ones.

10. Send Messages to Follow Up If You Want Your Career Networking To Be Successful

  • A brief message of gratitude goes a long way. So, make sure you don't forget to reiterate your feelings.
  • Within 24 to 48 hours, follow up.
  • Keep it brief, courteous, and unforgettable.
  • Before the moment passes, take this step to strengthen your new relationship.

11. Have faith in the procedure

  • It takes time to network. Not every interaction produces effects right away.
  • Continue to be consistent in your networking journey. You will get better the more you start practising.
  • Have patience and be receptive to new experiences. Years later, some connections might become friends, mentors, or collaborators.

How can students improve their networking skills?

Networking is an art that improves with time. You're already surrounded by opportunities as a resident at Urban Hub, including spots on the property, such as study lounges and social areas, and a diverse community that brings together people with various goals and viewpoints. As your well-wisher, we advise you to start early, be sincere, maintain your curiosity, and carefully cultivate your relationships. One of the most effective strategies for influencing your academic path, professional development, and future career success is networking, provided you approach it with purpose and sincerity. So, be wise with your communication, and happy networking residents!

FAQs

1. Why is networking important for students when starting their careers?

Networking helps students learn about absolute career paths, gain industry insights, and access opportunities that are often not advertised publicly.

2. How can university students build professional networks with no work experience?

Students can start by attending university events, joining societies, connecting with alumni, and engaging with professionals on platforms like LinkedIn.

3. What are the best networking platforms for students in the UK?

LinkedIn is one of the most widely used professional platforms, while university career portals, alumni networks, and platforms like Handshake are also popular in the UK.

4. How can introverted students network effectively without feeling uncomfortable?

Introverted students can focus on one-to-one conversations, online networking, and thoughtful follow-ups rather than extensive group interactions.

5. Can networking really help students secure internships and graduate jobs?

Yes, strong networks often lead to referrals, early information about roles, and personal recommendations, which can significantly improve job prospects.

item.title: Hidden Costs in Student Accommodation Most Students Don’t Expect
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Introduction
  2. Student Accommodation Costs to Be Careful of
  3. How to Manage Your Budget for Student Housing
  4. What Makes Urban Hub Unique
  5. In conclusion
  6. FAQs

Introduction

Rent is definitely the most significant expense when you move to a new place, but it is rarely the only expense. Many students become aware of this after they move in, when unforeseen living costs for students begin to mount and strain their finances. If you are unprepared, hidden costs in student accommodation might gradually drain your finances. These costs include utilities, internet upgrades, deposits, and end-of-tenancy fees, which often catch students off guard and strain their budget. You may prepare more effectively, reduce stress, and choose accommodation more wisely if you are aware of these expenses beforehand. Today, let's take a closer look at the hidden costs students don't usually anticipate, broken down below, along with tips for managing your finances.

Student Accommodation Costs to Be Careful of

Utility Bills

  • Rent does not necessarily include gas, electricity or water.
  • Depending on consumption, fees may be charged monthly or quarterly.
  • Wintertime heating often leads to higher costs.
  • If usage varies, shared housing may result in uneven expenses.

Internet and Wi-Fi

  • Budgeted accommodation may not have internet access or may have slow connections.
  • For reliable online lectures, research, and submissions, students may need to upgrade their devices.
  • Long-term contracts or installation fees may increase expenses.

Insurance for Your Belongings

  • Is not always covered by student housing.
  • Safeguards valuables like phones, gaming consoles, and laptops.
  • It may be vital whether you're looking for protection against theft, damage, or unintentional loss.

Administrative Fees and Deposits

Students could have to pay:
  • A security deposit for the property.
  • A tenancy deposit is required before relocation.
  • Even if the majority of administrative fees have been restricted, there may still be extra costs.
  • Always verify the amount and circumstances of refunds.

Cleaning or damage fees at the end of the tenancy

Deductions from student rent in the UK may be made if the property is not returned in good, clean, and excellent condition. There may be fees for:
  • Expert cleaning.
  • Wall markings or carpet stains.
  • Furniture that is missing or broken.
  • Unfair claims can be prevented by taking pictures during check-in.

Confusion About Council Tax

Students enrolled full-time are typically exempt. Fees might be incurred if:
  • You reside with non-students.
  • In the middle of your tenure, you either graduate or drop out.
  • Bills may become outdated if the council is not kept current.

Fees for Storage or Summer Rent

If you stay during the summer, hidden costs in student accommodation UK are bound to happen:
  • You could have to pay rent outside term time.
  • Double rent may arise from overlapping contracts.
  • If you leave anything behind, storage costs might be incurred.

How to Manage Your Budget for Student Housing

Ask the Right Questions Before Signing

  • Which expenses are covered by the rent?
  • Are there any extra fees during or following the lease?
  • If the situation changes, who is responsible for the council tax?

Make Use of Budgeting Resources

  • Tracking spending can be helped by student budgeting apps or online resources.
  • It's usually a good idea to set aside money for unforeseen expenses.

Record Everything

  • On the day of move-in, take old pictures and movies.
  • Report any damage immediately to avoid additional fees.

What Makes Urban Hub Unique

Urban Hub is a firm believer in total transparency, unlike many accommodation providers. We don't conceal any unexpected student housing expenses. The only sum you have to worry about is your rent; there are no unforeseen add-ons that come up later. As a result, our residents can properly budget their money without worrying about any hidden electricity bills, internet upgrades, or last-minute expenses. You may focus on your studies and university life rather than paperwork or hidden costs, as your stay with Urban Hub is designed to be safe, secure, and entirely burden-free.

In conclusion

Although extra charges in student accommodation are ordinary, they don't have to be unexpected. Students can minimise unnecessary financial stress and focus on their academics by carefully preparing, asking the right questions, and selecting transparent housing providers. At Urban Hub, life as a student is straightforward, uncomplicated, and stress-free. Because of this, our accommodations are designed with transparency in mind, allowing students to budget with confidence and avoid unforeseen expenses. You may make wise decisions and have a more seamless, comfortable time as a student by being aware of the actual cost of student housing.

FAQs

1. Does the rent for student housing include utility bills?

Depending on the supplier, yes. While some lodgings offer all-inclusive rent, others require students to pay their own utility bills.

2. Does the UK require students to pay council tax?

Full-time students are often exempt, however if you leave your course mid-tenancy or live with non-students, there may be fees.

3. What is a refundable tenancy deposit?

Before moving in, tenants must pay a tenancy deposit, which is recoverable if the property is returned undamaged.

4. As a student, do I require a TV licence?

Yes, whether you use BBC iPlayer on any device, including a phone or laptop, or view or stream live TV.

5. How can I prevent unforeseen fees when my lease expires?

Keep the property tidy and well-maintained, take dated pictures upon check-in, and report any damage right away.

item.title: Student Accommodation Rules: International Students Often Don’t Know
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Introduction
  2. Student Council Tax Regulations
  3. The Legal Protection of Deposits
  4. Legal rules for student accommodation UK
  5. Bills Might Not Always Be Included
  6. Rent checks are required.
  7. Guidelines for Guests and Subletting
  8. Upkeep and Reporting Obligations
  9. In Conclusion- Student accommodation rules for international students UK
  10. FAQs

Introduction

As an international or first-year student, moving to the UK is exciting. However, as it may be your first time living away from home, it is important to understand how student housing regulations work in the UK. Many students focus mainly on rental costs, only to realise later that living in the UK involves specific rules, legal requirements, and practical considerations such as distance, convenience, and amenities, for which they are often unprepared. Early awareness of these guidelines can help you settle in more easily, save money, and reduce stress.

In the context above, let's discuss the essential student accommodation rules that international students should be aware of but are often unaware of.

Student Council Tax Regulations

In the UK, full-time students are typically not subject to council tax. The exemption applies only if everyone in the property is a full-time student. You must provide the local council with a valid student status certificate confirming your enrolment. Council tax may be payable if:

  • You live with one or more non-students.
  • If you withdraw from your course or graduate mid-tenancy.
  • To avoid backdated charges, it falls on you to always notify the council as soon as possible.

The Legal Protection of Deposits

Tenancy deposits, typically up to five weeks' rent, are required for most student housing. These deposits must be protected under a government-approved tenancy deposit scheme, as required by law. Doing so will protect you from unfair deductions at the conclusion of your lease. Another important aspect of this protection is that you receive written confirmation of where your deposit is protected within 30 days.

Legal rules for student accommodation UK

A tenancy agreement is enforceable once it is signed, regardless of whether you are still in the United Kingdom. After you sign, if your plans change, you should carefully review the following:

  • Cancellation provisions (particularly in cases of delayed visas).
  • Tenancy duration and terms of termination.
  • Penalties and payment schedules.
  • Verbal pledges should not be relied upon; only the written terms of the contract are important.

Bills Might Not Always Be Included

Utility bills are not always included in student accommodation. And in these cases, you might have to pay more for amenities like:

  • Water, gas, and electricity.
  • Wi-Fi upgrades or additional internet packages.
  • TV licence (needed for BBC iPlayer or live TV).

Budgeting can be easier, and unexpected expenses can be avoided, if you choose an all-inclusive student accommodation such as Urban Hub.

Rent checks are required.

Landlords and student accommodation providers in the UK are required to perform Right to Rent checks. While doing so, international students UK are required to provide:

  • A current passport.
  • Documentation about immigration status or visas.
  • Landlords are legally unable to rent to you without these checks.

Guidelines for Guests and Subletting

Generally speaking, subletting is prohibited without written consent. A lot of student housing has:

  • Policies for guests.
  • Quiet hours or noise restrictions.
  • Restrictions on staying overnight.
  • Tenancy termination or warnings may result from breaking these restrictions.

Breaching these UK housing laws international students may face warnings or even termination of their tenancy. If you plan to host non-resident guests, it is best to follow accommodation rules and seek permission where required.

Upkeep and Reporting Obligations

Tenants are required to report any maintenance issues promptly.

As a resident, it is your responsibility as a tenant to take charge of the place you are residing in. You must take charge of:

  • Keeping your room or studio tidy.
  • Take care to avoid damage beyond normal wear and tear.
  • To prevent unjust end-of-tenancy fees, take pictures when you check in.

In Conclusion: Student Accommodation Rules for International Students in the UK

To ensure a stress-free university experience, it is essential to understand UK student housing laws. Understanding these housing regulations helps international students avoid common pitfalls and unexpected costs.

At Urban Hub, life as a student is straightforward, open, and encouraging. We make sure your stay is hassle-free, safe, and comfortable with clear contracts, all-inclusive pricing, secure premises, and student-focused services. With Urban Hub by your side, you can concentrate on what really matters- your studies and your time as a student in the UK.

Wishing you a smooth and comfortable student housing experience in the UK. Happy housing buddies!

FAQs

1. Does the UK require foreign students to pay council tax?

Unless they move in with a non-student or alter their student status, the majority of full-time students are exempt.

2. Is there legal protection for my tenancy deposit?

Yes, deposits must be made in a program approved by the government and verified within 30 days.

3. After I sign the contract, can I end my tenancy?

Unless there is a break provision or an explicit termination term, a signed tenancy is legally binding.

4. Does the rent for student housing include utility bills?

Not necessarily; unless otherwise specified, many homes charge separately for utilities and a TV licence.

5. Can I rent my student housing or host visitors?

Subletting is typically forbidden without written consent, and guest stays are restricted.

item.title: Is Preston Still an Affordable City for Students in 2026?
item.dc:creator: Parul
item.content:encoded:
Table of Contents

  1. Introduction
  2. A City Made for Students
  3. Good Employment Prospects for Students
  4. Affordable Accommodation Options for Preston student living
  5. Strategic Placement of Urban Hub
  6. Social Life and Entertainment at a Reasonable Price
  7. The year 2026 calls for a wise decision!
  8. FAQs

Introduction

When selecting a university city, you must consider the cost. Preston has long been considered more affordable than many other UK university cities. It is one of the top UK student cities for affordability. Although the cost of living has risen across the UK in recent years, Preston remains comparatively affordable. In this scenario, one question remains on students’ minds: Is Preston affordable for students in 2026? Simply put, Preston remains one of the most affordable student cities in the UK, where students can live at a reasonable cost. It is a small city with good living conditions at a lower price than in other major UK university cities. The city has both essential amenities and a welcoming atmosphere. Students and residents find it relatively easy to travel around the city. Moreover, they can enjoy food options and nightlife within their budget.

A City Made for Students

One of the most attractive points of Preston for students is its walkability! The city is so small that you will not have any difficulty traversing the main areas, such as lecture theatres, the city centre, shops, cafés, and Preston railway station. Besides, all this is very advantageous to students as they do not need to spend a lot of money on daily commuting. The city is well-connected, with frequent trains to Manchester, Liverpool, and London, among others. As a result, taking a trip and visiting places over the weekend is quite easy.

Good Employment Prospects for Students

Being in the very centre of Preston is a huge benefit for students, as they quickly get part-time jobs. Preston offers students part-time employment in various fields, including shops and restaurants. They are quite accessible and very friendly to students. The main benefits of these jobs are easy access and great flexibility, making it very convenient for students to manage their study and work schedules and thus avoid many challenges. Furthermore, the University of Central Lancashire (UCLan) facilitates part-time on-campus jobs for students during the academic year.​

Affordable Accommodation Options for Preston student living

The student cost of living UK, is generally the biggest bite of the students' money pie. However, this is precisely the point at which Preston wins over the students! Preston's rental values are very low for the UK, making it one of the areas with the lowest cost of living. Therefore, Preston is the top destination for students, whether they are freshers or returning students. There are several types of accommodation for students to pick from: private student accommodation, shared houses, or university halls, depending on their preferences. These options are fantastic because they fit the students' budgets and lifestyles. It is a common choice for students after the first year to move into private student housing or share a house with friends, which, on the whole, enables them to significantly cut their rent and utilities.

Strategic Placement of Urban Hub

Students do not need to worry about money, as Urban Hub provides well-equipped accommodation at an all-inclusive price. Our locations are really convenient, which contributes to the low cost of living, allowing students to focus on their studies and careers without worrying about their accommodation.

Social Life and Entertainment at a Reasonable Price

In a student's life, creating memories is just as important as attending lectures and completing coursework! Preston certainly ranks among the top cheap cities for students in the UK, and its lively, vibrant nightlife is one of the reasons, along with its low cost. The price of a pint is still lower than the average UK price, and there are a significant number of cafés, bars, and nightclubs in Preston for students with every taste. For example, UCLan students can hang out at Lampworks and other social spots to rest and enjoy the company of friends, as these spots are not too pricey.

The year 2026 calls for a wise decision!

In a nutshell, the UK's student cities have seen price hikes, yet Preston remains one of the most affordable, convenient, and high-quality-of-life cities for students. Urban Hub would be your ideal choice if you have made up your mind on Preston and are still searching for budget-friendly living. Our studio apartments are booking fast, so make your reservation now!

FAQs

1. In 2026, is Preston still among the UK's most affordable cities for students?

Yes, Preston is still one of the most affordable cities in the UK for students, especially compared to larger cities like Birmingham, Manchester, and London.

2. How much does Preston's student housing cost?

With alternatives ranging from shared housing to purpose-built student housing at competitive weekly prices, Preston's student housing costs are often lower than the national average.

3. Is it easy for students to find part-time work in Preston?

Indeed, there are many student-friendly part-time jobs in retail, hospitality, and on-campus positions at UCLan in Preston.

4. Is Preston a student-friendly city?

Indeed. Because Preston is a small, walkable city, students don't need to rely heavily on public transportation to get to college, stores, transportation hubs, or social areas.

5. Do international students find Preston to be a decent city?

Yes, Preston is well-liked by overseas students because of its reasonable living expenses, friendly locals, convenient transport and robust student support services.

  8. Conclusion: Preston Is the Smart Student Choice
  9. FAQs

Introduction

The factors that influence choosing a university in a suitable city have evolved and are no longer confined to the university's ranking and reputation alone. Students today are factoring in considerations such as lifestyle, mental health, cost of living, and community feeling. They are still attracting many students, but big UK student cities like Birmingham, Manchester, and London are now often replaced by Preston in many students' choices.

But why this change?

In this blog guide, we will discuss the benefits of living in Preston as a student for a complete university experience without the daily hassles of larger cities.

A Student City That Feels Manageable, Not Overwhelming

Preston's size is among its main advantages. Students love how easy it is to study in Preston. To explain better, here's why:

Compact and highly walkable

  • Most of the lecture halls, dormitories, shops, cafés, and the city centre are walkable.
  • Students not only save money but also time by reducing their use of public transport.

Easy to adjust

  • Preston is not busy or crowded like the larger cities.
  • Students get to know the town quickly, which helps them feel at home.

Strong Academic Opportunities at UCLan

The University of Central Lancashire (UCLan) is the main reason students are in Preston.

Academic reputation recognised

  • UCLan is one of the best universities in the North West region.
  • The university is particularly famous for courses like business, engineering, forensic science, and health.

A student-centred approach to the city results in

  • very high student satisfaction.
  • a strong focus on practical learning and employability.
  • student-friendly ambience.

The city of Preston offers many students a high-quality education that meets their needs, while also keeping their minds free of the competition and high costs associated with living in a big city.

Affordable Living Without Compromising on Quality

The cost of living is one of the criteria students consider most, and this is where Preston excels.

Rent prices are lower than in the bigger cities.

  • Co-living and student apartments are much cheaper than in othe, whichr places.
  • The management of utilities, food, and day-to-day expenses is also easier to deal with.

Greater cost-effectiveness

  • The students have accommodation options near the university, and at a reasonable price.
  • The reduction in financial pressure allows students to give more time to academics and socialisation.
  • The city's walkability makes it very convenient for students, as they don't have to spend much on their daily commute.

With the rising cost of living, Preston offers comfort to parents and students.

A Social Life Designed for Students

Preston is one of the smaller cities in the UK, but it has a very livable student life.

Nights out that won’t break the bank.

  • Nightlife in bars, pubs, and clubs is student-friendly and affordable.

Food scene in the area

  • From independent cafes to international cuisine, students can go out for meals without exceeding their budget.
  • No financial burden is attached to students, and they enjoy all the perks of a university city.

Green Spaces, Culture, and Things to Do

Preston does not just offer lectures and nightlife; it provides much more.

Nature and outdoor spaces

  • Avenham and Miller Parks are great places for walks and relaxation during study breaks.
  • The Guild Wheel provides a variety of cycling and walking options around the city.

Culture on a budget

  • The Harris Museum and local art galleries offer free or inexpensive cultural experiences.
  • Flag Market is a place where events, food stalls, and community gatherings are regularly held.

All these things, including nature, culture, and affordability, help create a perfect student lifestyle to be enjoyed and experienced.

Urban Hub: Supporting a Smarter Student Choice

At Urban Hub, we recognise the reason why Preston is attractive to the current student population. As a result, we offer living studios that cater to almost every need, whether you want to go solo or stay in shared places. We offer-

Purpose-built student accommodation

  • Student-specific smart, cosy, and stylish living spaces.
  • The total price system helps students manage their expenses more effectively.

Convenient locations

  • Near UCLan and the city centre.
  • Quick travel, fewer problems, and more time for the important things.

Urban Hub stands beside Preston student life that seeks living conditions that are up to the mark, without paying extra for what is not needed.

Conclusion: Preston Is the Smart Student Choice

In light of this, a famous university, reasonable living expenses, a lively social life, and quality student housing are all contributing to Preston's reputation as the best smaller UK cities for students where size does not matter.

If students want a university life with no financial or mental stress, it is not just an option Preston offers; it is the smartest choice. Furthermore, Urban Hub handles finding the right place for you, so it's one less issue to deal with.

FAQs

1. Is Preston a good city for international students in the UK?

Preston offers affordable living, a welcoming community, quality education, and a student-friendly environment for international students.

2. How much does it cost to live in Preston as a student compared to London or Manchester?

Living in Preston is significantly cheaper, with lower rent, transport costs, and everyday expenses than in bigger cities.

3. What makes UCLan a popular choice for students in the North West of England?

UCLan offers career-focused courses, strong industry connections, modern facilities, and high student satisfaction.

4. Is Preston safe and easy to get around for university students?

Preston is a compact, walkable city with safe neighbourhoods, reliable transport, and student-focused amenities.

5. What is the best student accommodation near UCLan in Preston?

Purpose-built student accommodation near UCLan offers modern studios, affordability, convenience, and inclusive utility packages.
